- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment history shows no positive sentiment (all 0.00), model tends to overreact to recent price drops; apply a downward bias correction of 0.5–1.5% to the first 5–7 forecast days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 10-day average), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2.0% below the immediate prior high.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; if 10-day average is >10% above recent 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment history with 0.00 values suggests low market confidence; model should not assume upward momentum; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to all forecast days unless sentiment turns positive.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction; delay correction by 1–2 days if sentiment remains flat; adjust only after 3–5 consecutive days of flat or negative sentiment.
